en: to be slim; to be slender; to be fragile

examples.en: That singer has a delicate voice.
She carried a heavy load on her slender shoulders.
She looks slight, but she's strong.
She spoke in a faintly trembling voice.
My fingers are slender, so rings are too big.
The frail child has become healthy before I knew it.

explain: 몸이나 목소리, 줄기가 가늘고 연약해 보일 때 써요. '날씬하다'와 달리 약하고 섬세해 보이는 느낌이 있어요. 보통 '가녀린 몸', '가녀린 목소리'처럼 사람이나 식물에 말해요.

phrases.en: My wrists are slender, so the ring is too big.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸의 가늘고 약해 보이는 부분에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: It suits thin, delicate-looking parts of the body.

phrases.en: A flower bloomed on the slender stem.
phrases.nuance_en: It also works for thin plant stems.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 가녀려 보여도 힘이 세요.
phrases.en: That person looks slender but is strong.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습의 인상을 말할 때 '~아/어 보이다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '~아/어 보이다' to describe a visual impression.

explain_en: It describes a body, voice or stem that is thin and looks fragile. Unlike '날씬하다' (slim), it carries a feeling of being delicate and weak. It is typically used as in '가녀린 몸' and '가녀린 목소리', for people or plants.

examples.en: A dazzling brilliance came from the jewel.
I polished the shoes hard until they shone.
I want to have glowing skin.

examples.ko: 달빛 아래 호수가 은은한 광채를 띠었어요.
examples.en: Under the moonlight, the lake took on a soft glow.
Even though this painting is old, its brilliance is the same.

examples.ko: 눈부신 광채에 나도 모르게 눈을 감았어요.
examples.en: I closed my eyes without realizing it at the dazzling light.

explain: 그냥 '빛'보다 반짝이며 눈부신 빛을 말해요. '광채가 나다', '광채를 띠다'처럼 쓰고, 눈빛이나 얼굴에서 느껴지는 생기도 비유해요. 물건 표면이 반들반들한 윤기는 '광택'이라고 해서 구분해요.

phrases.example: 그 반지는 불빛 아래에서 광채가 나요.
phrases.en: That ring sparkles under the light.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation with 광채.

phrases.example: 기쁜 날에는 그의 눈이 광채를 띠었어요.
phrases.en: On happy days his eyes shone brightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈이나 얼굴에서 생기가 느껴질 때처럼 비유로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Also used figuratively, for a lively look in the eyes or face.

phrases.en: The new shoes have a nice shine and look pretty.
phrases.nuance_en: The smooth glossy shine of a surface is called 광택.

explain_en: Rather than plain '빛', it means a sparkling, dazzling light. It is used as '광채가 나다' or '광채를 띠다', and it also figuratively describes the vitality seen in eyes or a face. The smooth shine of a surface is '광택', which is a separate word.

examples.en: The skirt flutters in the wind.
A butterfly fluttered over and landed on my shoulder.
The loose shirt flaps back and forth.
The child runs off with a scarf fluttering behind.
The towels dance on the clothesline.
The hem of the coat fluttered.

explain: 얇은 천이나 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 흔들리는 모양이에요. 뒤에 '날리다, 흔들리다, 움직이다' 같은 동사가 잘 와요.

phrases.en: Her hair flutters in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가벼운 것이 바람에 자꾸 날리는 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something light being blown around by the wind.

phrases.en: The laundry sways in the wind.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천이 계속 흔들리는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
나비나 새가 가볍게 날개를 흔들며 나는 모습에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a butterfly or bird flying with lightly flapping wings.

explain_en: It describes thin cloth or light things moving back and forth in the wind. Verbs like '날리다', '흔들리다' and '움직이다' often follow it.

examples.en: The child is sitting quietly and demurely on the chair.
She sat demurely with her legs together.
The bride bowed her head modestly and greeted everyone.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 어른들 말씀을 다소곳이 들었어요.
examples.en: That child listened meekly to what the adults said.

examples.ko: 꾸중을 들은 동생이 다소곳이 서 있어요.
examples.en: My younger sibling, who got scolded, is standing there quietly.

examples.ko: 손을 모은 채 다소곳이 차례를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: With hands folded, I waited my turn quietly.

explain: 앉다, 서다, 고개를 숙이다, 듣다처럼 조용한 동작과 자주 함께 써요. 얌전하고 공손한 태도를 그릴 때 쓰는 말이라, 소리 내지 않고 조용히 있는 모습에 어울려요.

phrases.en: She sat quietly and modestly on the chair and waited.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가장 흔한 짝말로 얌전하게 앉은 모습을 그려요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, picturing someone sitting demurely.

phrases.nuance_ko: 조용하고 공손하게 서 있는 모습에 써요.

phrases.en: The child bowed their head politely and said hello.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예의 바른 인사나 부끄러운 모습에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a polite greeting or a shy gesture.

explain_en: It often goes with quiet actions such as sitting, standing, bowing the head and listening. It paints a gentle, respectful attitude, so it suits someone who stays calm and quiet.

en: to be slippery; to be slimy

examples.en: There's oil on the floor, so it's slippery.
The soap keeps feeling slippery in my hand.

examples.ko: 생선을 만졌더니 손이 미끈거려서 바로 씻었어요.
examples.en: My hands felt slimy after touching the fish, so I washed them right away.

examples.ko: 샤워 후에도 몸이 미끈거리면 물로 더 헹궈 보세요.
examples.en: If your body still feels slimy after a shower, try rinsing more with water.
After I wiped the slippery bathroom floor, it was fine.

examples.ko: 이 샴푸는 헹굴 때 좀 미끈거리지만 금방 없어져요.
examples.en: This shampoo feels a bit slick when you rinse it, but it goes away soon.

explain: 기름, 비누, 점액처럼 물기나 미끄러운 막이 있어서 손이나 몸에 닿는 느낌을 말할 때 써요. '미끄럽다'가 넘어질 수 있는 바닥 같은 데 잘 어울린다면, '미끈거리다'는 닿는 감촉에 더 초점이 있어요. '미끌거리다'도 비슷한 느낌으로 써요.

phrases.en: The handle is slippery because there's oil on it.
Seaweed feels slimy when you touch it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '느낌'을 꾸며 촉감을 설명할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often modifies 느낌 to describe how something feels.

phrases.en: My hands feel slippery after using detergent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸에 닿은 미끄러운 감촉을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a slippery feel on the body.

explain_en: It describes how something feels to the touch when it has a film of oil, soap or mucus. '미끄럽다' fits a floor you could fall on, while '미끈거리다' focuses more on the feel against your skin. '미끌거리다' is used with a similar feel.
